transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what brings me in is that I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. Even when it's really important. 

I work in IT support, and... I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and ten minutes later I'll realize I've reread the exact same log entries three times. And I still don't even know what they say. It's just getting impossible to get through my work.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself moving around, even when you're trying to focus on a task?

Yeah, I do. It's... well, even when I'm supposed to just sit still and listen, it feels like there's a motor humming under my skin. I just get this constant urge like I need to stand up, check something, or move on to the next problem right that second. It makes it really hard to just stay in my chair.
When did you first start noticing these kinds of problems with focus and restlessness? Were they present when you were a child, or did they come on more recently?

Well, it's definitely not a recent thing. It's been there since I was a kid. Actually, my mother still jokes about my old grade school report cards. She says the teachers always wrote that I was bright, but I could never stay in my seat. I was always blurting out answers before the teacher finished the question, and I'd lose my homework all the time... even when I had actually done it. So yeah, it's been going on pretty much my whole life.
